title: Playing dances with his brother Dean
summary: At about fifteen he and drummer brother Dean played all the local dances for two or three dollars a night.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: So you say you went about, when you did you play -- started to work, let's say. What kind of jobs, dances, parties.
I had a -- my brother and I -- my brother was a drummer and I had a little band.
You had a brother who was a drummer?
Yeah, we --
What was his name?
Dean Howard. And he and I used to play dances at night.
About how old were you then?
Round about -- I was about, let me see if I can get my age straightened out. I was just a little kid running around the streets.
About 16.
Yeah, about 15.
You and your brother had a little band?
Yeah, we had a little band.
Did you call it the Howard Brothers or anything?
No, not the Howard Brothers, just a band. Dean and Paul, that's it. We played in all of the dances that were played in town. People would come and listen
to us.
They would come? So were you making money at that point, or was it like for free?
Yeah, but very little money.
What was your take for the night, do you have an idea.
A night, oh, yeah, about $2.00. $2.00 or $3.00 a night, we didn't get much money, but it was quite interesting what we were doing and I enjoyed it very much.
That was great experience too.
At that time did you have what they called the kitty?
Yeah, they had a kitty.
Did would that work out pretty good.
No, it didn't work out too good.
Did they ever throw money at you and try to hit you (unintelligible)?
Yep, they'd try to hit you. They'd try to hit you and all like that. When they tried to get me, I'd hit 'em back. I would.
You must have been a pretty fiery little guy with the hands, you would take them on if they bothered you.
